question: Religious-name recipients absent from every IRS bulk file: for a stratified sample of the 14,772 top-50 recipient EINs with church/synagogue/parish-type names and no trace in the BMF, Pub 78, revocation list, e-Postcard data or TEOS index ($1.35bn DAF-weighted), check whether each is a group-ruling subordinate (e.g. Official Catholic Directory) or a congregation that never applied, using the central organisation's published directory and the BMF GROUP field of the parent
conclusion_affected: Size of the 'unresolved' bucket (76% of non-BMF dollars on the task's six-way split); whether church-status dollars in the CN-eligibility denominator are understated
rationale: Churches need not apply or file and group subordinates need not be listed individually, so absence from IRS files is expected rather than suspicious; but 2,360 of these EINs ($0.24bn) carry a name that matches exactly one same-state BMF EIN, so some are wrong EINs. Only a directory check separates the two

question: Disregarded-entity recipients: confirm from the parent's Form 990 Schedule R Part I (identification of disregarded entities) that the four CZ Biohub / CZ Imaging Institute LLC EINs ($1.59bn DAF-weighted, 38% of non-BMF dollars) and the other 55 LLC-named recipients are disregarded entities of a 501(c)(3), and record the parent EIN so DAF dollars can be re-attributed to a BMF organisation
conclusion_affected: CN-eligible share of top-50 DAF dollars (76.9%); recipient concentration figures
rationale: LLC names are only a name rule here. Re-attributing $1.59bn to a parent would move about 2.2 points of top-50 DAF-weighted dollars out of 'not in BMF'

question: Revoked-at-grant reconciliation: for the 141 recipient EINs whose automatic revocation took effect before the granting sponsor's fiscal year began ($7.24m DAF-weighted), re-check the revocation list monthly for retroactive reinstatements and look up TEOS determination letters; report how much remains revoked after reinstatements, split by whether the same organisation is listed under a newer EIN
conclusion_affected: The revoked-at-grant-time figure and its framing as a sponsor due-diligence signal
rationale: Revocations can be reinstated retroactively to the revocation date (IRS reinstatement page), and $1.87m of the $6.33m posted before the fiscal year went to names now listed under another EIN (stale EIN, money probably reached a recognised successor). The figure is a public-data screen, not a finding of improper grants

question: Grant-date precision for the revoked-at-grant test: parse sponsor-level grant dates where public (sponsor grant-search tools or annual reports for the 30 sponsors with before-FY lines) to replace the fiscal-year window with actual grant dates for the 'during fiscal year' bucket (272 EINs, $11.30m)
rationale: Schedule I dates grants only to the sponsor's fiscal year; 'during FY' lines could fall either side of the revocation date

question: Earlier BMF extracts: obtain a dated 2023 or 2024 IRS EO BMF snapshot (the IRS page offers only the current files) from an archive that preserves the IRS files unchanged, with a robots check, and re-run the non-BMF classification to separate organisations dropped from the BMF after FY2023-24 from those never listed
conclusion_affected: Split between 'merged or terminated' / 'revoked after grant' and 'never listed'; CN-eligibility at grant time rather than in November 2026
rationale: The task asked for earlier BMF extracts from IRS bulk downloads; www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/exempt-organizations-business-master-file-extract-eo-bmf lists only current files (plus 2016-2017 SIT files, pre-2021), so this pass relied on final-return flags and revocation dates instead

question: Recipients with filings but no BMF row and no revocation (170 EINs, $46.9m, e.g. a sports-team foundation and a closed arts university): check TEOS determination letters and the latest return's Part V/Schedule N for status changes, and test whether the BMF omission is a monthly-file lag by re-reading the December 2026 BMF
conclusion_affected: Residual unresolved bucket among the 1213 CN filing-rule passers (126 of them; $43.4m)
rationale: These are the only non-BMF EINs with live e-filing and no termination or revocation signal in any IRS bulk file
